==Starting off==
{{Needed|[[Vyre noble outfit]], [[Blisterwood flail]] or {{Coins|40000}} to buy the [[blisterwood flail]], combat supplies.|recommended=[[Food]] and [[Prayer potions]], [[Drakan's medallion]].}}
[[File:Sarius Guile chathead.png|left]]
[[File:Makeshift shrine.png|thumb|140px|Ivan's shrine to the fallen Myreque.]]
Make your way to the [[Icyene Graveyard]], accessed via the boat in the southernmost part of [[Burgh de Rott]] or [[Meiyerditch]], or south-west of [[Slepe]]. Once there, speak to [[Sarius Guile]], who will inform you that she is leaving [[Morytania]] soon. She will tell you that Vanescula left behind some money for her in case of emergencies, which she will use to pay mercenaries from [[Misthalin]] for safe passage.

Sarius will mention that the kidnapped Myreque member [[Safalaan Hallow|Safalaan]] and Sarius' mistress [[Vanescula Drakan|Vanescula]] are being held prisoner by [[Lowerniel Drakan]] in [[Castle Drakan|his castle]]. She'll also share that all vampyres have been ordered to attend a gathering outside the castle for an announcement in regards to the future. Finally, she'll ask that you try to help Vanescula, who Sarius says has always been good towards her. You will tell her that you'll do what you can, and that you need to go find [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]].

Make your way to the [[Myreque_Hideout#South_Meiyerditch|Myreque Hideout]] in Meiyerditch, located under [[Old Man Ral]]'s house ({{Map|type=maplink|x=3607|y=3208|mtype=pin}}), to find a [[makeshift shrine]]. Inspect it to initiate a [[cutscene]] where Ivan will arrive. You will inform him of Drakan's announcement and Safalaan's imprisonment, and despite his initial hesitance, he will eventually agree to come with you.<!--Memories of the Myreque unlocks with cutscene--> If you haven't already, search the chest to the north to pick up a set of [[vyre noble clothing]], and buy a flail if you don't already have one.

Before you make your way to Castle Drakan, bring food and prayer potions, as you'll be protecting yourself and Ivan from multiple [[vyrewatch]] and [[Vyrewatch Sentinel|sentinels]] for several minutes. Once you're ready, equip the vyre noble clothing, then speak to Ivan to depart and initiate a cutscene.<!--Gathering unlocks with the announcement cutscene-->

===The crowd goes wild===
[[File:Lowerniel Drakan chathead.png|left]]
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - Drakan's announcement.png|thumb|300px|Drakan addresses his subjects, with Safalaan and Vanescula in tow.]]
Upon arriving at Castle Drakan, Vanescula and Safalaan can be seen hanging unconscious before the crowd. Drakan will arrive, proclaiming the [[vampyre]] race has been weakened by becoming civilised and aristocratic; rather than the hunters they once were, they have now become no more than farmers. He will announce that he has found a way to return to their homeworld of [[Vampyrium]], and that he will return their race to one of hunters, rather than aristocrats. The nobles [[Lord Alexei Jovkai]] and [[Lord Mischa Myrmel]] will voice their scepticism and opposition, content with their lifestyle on Gielinor and telling him that he's welcome to take any that are deluded enough to follow him.

He will then announce the Night of the Blood Moon, a festival of hunting and carnage in which the vampyre with the most kills becomes the leader. The blood shed from this festival will supposedly provide the blood needed to enable mass transport for the remaining vampyres. Before he departs, he points out both you and Ivan to the crowd, ending the cutscene. 

Pray [[Protect from Melee]], and immediately attack the three [[vyrewatch]] to keep them from damaging Ivan, who is initially traumatised due to the previous events there. All enemies will change aggro to you when attacked, but will refocus on Ivan if they are unable to attack you for some time. Make note of this when safespotting the vyrewatch.

[[Acidic bloodveld|Acidic bloodvelds]] will begin to occasionally spawn. If they reach Ivan, they will explode for 25-30 damage onto him and any nearby targets, including the vyrewatch. You should still try to kill them before they reach him. As the battle goes on, [[Vyrewatch Sentinel|vyrewatch sentinels]] will also join the battle. Unlike the sentinels outside Darkmeyer, these sentinels attack using blood spells, healing them for a portion of damage dealt. Prioritise the sentinels while praying melee. After several minutes, Ivan will complete the spell, teleporting you both out of Castle Drakan and back to the hideout.

==The Truth Hurtz==
{{Needed|[[Pickaxe]] (obtainable from [[Ivan Strom]]) and [[combat]] supplies with [[Blisterwood flail]], including (but not necessarily required) [[Efaritay's aid]] to speed up [[vyrewatch]] kills.|recommended=[[Drakan's medallion]] or 10,000 [[coins]].}}
{{Map|name=Slepe|height=280|width=280|zoom=1|x=3724|y=3335|align=right|caption=Slepe, showing locations of the church, the pub, and Crombwick manor
|mtype:rectangle,x:3726,y:3359,rectX:26,rectY:18
|mtype:rectangle,x:3749,y:3297,rectX:9,rectY:11|
|mtype:rectangle,x:3739,y:3314,rectX:12,rectY:24}}
''Those with lower stats should consider bringing a method of stat restoration such as a super restore potion as the Monks of Zamorak below will lower your stats temporarily. Leave seven inventory spaces free and make sure you do not have a pet out.''

Now aware of Drakan's plans, a plan is formed to find a way to Vampyrium, rescue [[Safalaan]], return to Gielinor, then close the portal in order to permanently trap him in Vampyrium. However, when you ask [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]] about [[Veliaf]], Ivan will tell you not set your expectations too high, given that he abandoned you and Ivan. However, Ivan will mention that he heard he might be in the nearby town of [[Slepe]].

Make your way to Slepe, either by running north from [[Ver Sinhaza]], or by using the [[ectophial]] and paying [[Andras]] (at the docks north-east) 10,000 coins to row a boat nearby. Head to the graveyard by the [[Slepe church|church]] and speak to Ivan<!--({{Map|type=maplink|x=3729|y=3308|mtype=pin}})-->. He'll suggest that, as with most things in the game, a pub is usually the best place to start asking for someone's whereabouts. Make sure Ivan is following you to the pub.

Head south-east to the [[Rat & Bat]] and speak to [[Roy]], the bartender who replaced [[Carl]]. He will say that someone fitting Veliaf's description came in earlier and had quite a bit to drink; he'll also mention that he heard a commotion at [[Crombwick Manor]] shortly after that man's departure. As the doors to the manor remain locked, you'll have to enter the manor through the [[Sisterhood Sanctuary]], the same way you did during [[Sins of the Father]].

Go down the stairs of the building just south of the graveyard; then, head north until you reach a gate. Pass the gate; then, climb up the nearby ladder to reach the inside of the manor. Once inside, you will find a drunk Veliaf cleaning house; help speed him along by killing all the [[vyrewatch]] in the manor. All damage during this battle can be negated with [[Protect from Melee]].

Once the final vyrewatch has fallen, talk to Veliaf. You will inform him of Drakan's plans, and Ivan will reprimand him for losing faith in the cause. Ivan will then reveals to Veliaf that he discovered for himself that he was the descendant of [[Ivandis Seergaze]], a secret that Veliaf had kept from him his entire life. After a few harsh words, Ivan will leave for the [[Paterdomus Temple]].

===Legacy of Seergaze===
Make your way to [[Drezel]] in the [[Paterdomus Temple|temple basement]], which can be quickly reached via fairy ring ({{Fairycode|CKS}}). Speak to [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]], and after a brief conversation with Drezel, he'll give you a [[squire's journal]], which belonged to a squire that served Ivandis. The journal will share that after the river was blessed, Ivandis intended to kill Drakan himself, even though the [[Misthalin–Morytania War|war]] had already been won with the vampyres trapped east of the River Salve. The squire writes that Ivandis gave him a book before departing to Vampyrium, the contents of which reveal what the [[Seven Priestly Warriors]] did leading up to the [[River Salve]] being blessed. However, the squire notes that revelations from Ivandis' book horrified him so much that he regretted reading them. As ordered, he preserved Ivandis' writings, but chose to hide them somewhere within what would become Paterdomus, away from the public eye.

Return to Drezel, who will decry the squire's writings as heresy. Ivan will tell the player that to properly search the temple, the [[monks of Zamorak]] taking residence will need to be dealt with. Head west through the basement and up to the temple; then, kill all the monks. They can drain combat stats, but should not prove to be an issue after all the vyres you've killed so far.

Head upstairs and speak with Ivan. Then search through the bookcases for six (6) books (you'll need the squire's journal). You must now solve the first puzzle of the quest. Each of the books describes a person, and must be placed on their corresponding plinth. Each plinth sits in front of a stained-glass portrait that depicts the subject of one of the books.

From north to south:
* {{plink|Pious Proceedings}}
* {{plink|The Life of Friar}}
* {{plink|Scruffy notebook}}
* {{plink|From Misthalin to Morytania}}
* {{plink|Sarl's journal}}
* {{plink|Essiandar's notes}}

Upon placing the last book, they will disappear in a puff of smoke and a click will be heard from the desk behind Ivan, who then searches it. Speak to him to receive [[Ivandis' writings]], revealing the ritual to bless the Salve was derived from [[haemalchemy]], which caused Ivandis to begin the process of vampyrification. Refusing to become the very thing he and his comrades fought against, he resolved to find a way into Vampyrium, and either kill Drakan or die trying. After much scouting, a tunnel was found that went directly to Castle Drakan; however, nothing was heard since, and Ivandis likely passed in the ensuing fight against Drakan.

Speak to Ivan again to return to the mausoleum, where you will find a now sobered Veliaf. You will discuss what you've discovered to Veliaf, (Ivandis' vampyrification aside), and conclude the tunnel to [[Castle Drakan]] is most likely around Ivandis' tomb. Ask Veliaf to lead the way, and the three of you will be transported to the tomb.

===Inside job===
Inspect the blockage to the south; then, mine through it. If you didn't bring a pickaxe, speak to Ivan for a [[Bronze pickaxe|bronze one]]. Upon entering the blockage, you arrive in a cavern with railroads and mine carts filled with [[daeyalt ore]]. Head north-east to a tunnel and enter, where you will be attacked by [[vyrewatch]] and [[vyrewatch sentinel]]s. 

You must now kill multiple vyrewatch, including two (2) vyrewatch sentinels. The sentinels will periodically summon blood orbs, which increase their damage; the vyrewatches can be lured toward them, and will take heavy damage if they come into contact. Be sure to stay at least '''two tiles''' away from the orbs, or you will take damage as well. Pray [[Protect from Magic]], and take out the sentinels as fast as possible. 
If you die or teleport out of the fight, you can find it again by going back into the [[Myreque Hideout]] via the trapdoor directly south of the [[Hair of the Dog]] in [[Canifis]]. Once you enter the trapdoor, search the southern wall of the room to enter the caves, and enter the cave entrance that is immediately to the east.

After killing them all, you discover that you are in a daeyalt refinery, where the process of vampyrification takes place. You will inform the slaves of the way out, then arrive at a basement. Head out through the north exit and climb up the large stairs to arrive at Castle Drakan. Before continuing, pray at the vampyric shrine to the east to unlock the teleport back here via [[Drakan's medallion]].

==Escape from Castle Drakan==
===Supplies and death mechanics===
During your time in [[Vampyrium]], you will have access to unique supplies. Some of the supplies can be found as individual spawns or by searching chests in the castle. 

Players can obtain:
* [[Mysterious jerky]], a high-healing food.
* [[Smelly kebab]], a [[fast food]].
* [[Foul chunky potion]]s, a mix of [[super restore]] and [[prayer regeneration potion]]s.
* [[Putrid sticky potion]]s, the equivalent of [[stamina potion]]s.
* [[Rank frothy potion]]s, the equivalent of [[super combat potion]].
* [[Rancid slimy potion]]s, similar to a [[Saradomin brew]] but drains the same stats by 1 instead.
* [[Jar of congealed blood|Jars of congealed blood]], which immediately restores all [[Hitpoints]] and [[Prayer]]. Although only one of these may be taken from the supply chest at a time, more can be picked up throughout the castle regardless of how many you already have.
These supplies can only be used within Vampyrium and cannot be banked.

Additionally, before each major fight, there is an object (e.g. a tent or table, which can be looted for an unlimited number of the supplies). These supply locations are usually located near where you spawn following a death. During fights with [[Drakan]], players are supplied with unlimited quantities of the aforementioned Vampyrium combat supplies, allowing indefinite attempts at defeating him without needing to leave Vampyrium for supply runs. 

[[Death]] also differs here in that you will respawn at predetermined checkpoints with all your items kept. However, [[hardcore ironmen]] '''will''' still lose their status if they die at any point during the quest.

After entering the portal, you will arrive at Vampyrium. However, several [[Venator (The Blood Moon Rises)|venators]] will chase you, forcing you to split up and escape to another room.
<!--Castle Drakan track unlocks here -->
The [[world map]] icon will be replaced with one of the castle, which shows the rooms you've visited, unlocked doors, and puzzles left to solve. You must now complete a series of puzzles to incrementally unlock more parts of the castle.

While exploring the rooms, you may come upon a few creatures in them; initially [[sanguidae]], small fly-like monsters that are very accurate and initially deal light damage that gradually increases and will inflict a small [[bleed]] of 2 when they deal 4 damage and [[webbed-winged crow]]s, which are not initially aggressive but will eventually become so. The crows are always found in pairs, and killing one will cause the other to become enraged, attacking faster, harder and piercing through prayer. Finally, as more rooms are unlocked, venators will also appear. They will attack with [[melee]] up close and [[ranged]] from afar. They also have a special attack in which they will screech; if the player has an overhead [[protection prayer]] active when this occurs, they will clench their ears in pain, dealing light damage for three (3) ticks and delaying their attack by a few ticks. When a venator is killed, it is guaranteed to drop a piece of [[mysterious jerky]]. Most of the enemies can be ignored, and it is recommended to do so.

The castle will only contain a few of the aforementioned supplies - mostly jerky, foul and sticky potions, either on tables or by searching crates and chests. Items of interest will have a sparkle of light periodically emitting from them.

After destroying the blood stockpile, a cutscene will play where the five of you are ready to leave. Before you can do so, Lowerniel appears and shuts the portal down. However, missing the thrill of the hunt, he lets you out into the land of Vampyrium, giving you a brief head start before the hunt begins.
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - the hunt begins.png|center|thumb|700x700px|Drakan prepares for the hunt.]]

==Blood Hunt==
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - Vampyrium establishing shot.png|thumb|280x280px|The land of Vampyrium.]]
You'll now find yourself in the land of [[Vampyrium]], the ancient homeworld of the vampyres. Like in [[Drakan's Castle]], the area will contain multiple spawns of the same food and potions. A [[cutscene]] will play in which the group arrives at a bridge in the ruined village of [[Sangvesti]], and [[Vanescula]] will say that the nearby drawbridge needs to be lowered. 

You must now complete another series of connected steps to put the old cog on the drawbridge. While doing so, more supplies can be found in the ruins, such as [[jerky]] and potions, as well as [[smelly kebab]]s, which are equivalent to [[cooked karambwan]]s. Be warned that you may log out, but if you teleport out before repairing the drawbridge, the cog will not stay in inventory and you'll need to get it again.

You will no longer be allowed to enter the castle from Vampyrium. If you didn't already unlock the Castle Drakan teleport, you must return the same way you originally entered: go to the [[Myreque Hideout]] south of the pub in [[Canifis]], enter the first cave entrance to your right after passing the wall, and then, enter the next south-eastern cave entrance. Follow this path all the way to the red portal; then, pray to the shrine to unlock the Castle Drakan teleport.

===Crossing the drawbridge===
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - Sangvesti quest map.png|thumb|500px|A map of Sangvesti.]]
At the small building three houses east of the altar, enter the building from the south door to pick up the [[crank wheel]]. Afterward, make your way to the building north of the altar. There will be a crank base in front of the door for you to operate. Once you start operating the base, '''Drakan will begin his pursuit'''<!--Hunted unlocks here-->. Click the crank base several more times until the yellow bar fills up; then, quickly enter the door. Once inside, search the bookshelf for a [[dusty book]] and read it to receive a [[Vitur key]].

From this building, run all the way east until you see a set of Vitur doors. Enter to find various searchable objects that, when searched, show a combination lock with poorly secure passcodes, such as the passcode for the food being simply "FOOD". This hints to the passcode to the shed outside: "'''TOOLS'''". Once you enter the passcode, you will receive a pair of [[bolt cutters]].

Make your way to the building east of the altar (the one with a Vitur door on its south side); enter and take the [[Tooth half of key (The Blood Moon Rises)|tooth half of key]] from the table. Next, head to the building directly south of the well ([[File:Water source icon.png|link=]] map icon), enter through the chained doors from the north side; then, pick up the [[Loop half of key (The Blood Moon Rises)|loop half of key]] and combine the two halves for the [[Myrmel key]].

Depending on where [[Drakan]] is, you may wish to either exit this building from the north or south side to avoid him. Make your way to the building east of the well. Enter through the Myrmel door; then, pick up the [[bucket]] in the north-west corner. Fill it with [[water]] from the well outside; then, quickly return inside. Use the [[bucket of water]] on the northernmost barrel in the building to receive a [[Shadum key]].

Next, make your way to the building south-west of [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]] and the group, and enter through the Shadum door from the west side. Take the [[trapdoor key]] on the crate; then, make your way to the [[bank]] just south of the [[altar]]. Operate the crank base inside until the yellow bar fills; then, open the gate and enter the trapdoor. This will take you into the building with the altar.

In the dining room are five (5) chairs, which reveal a verse from an ancient religion when inspected. These verses hint at which prayer must be active in order to restore [[prayer points]] from the altar; for example, praying at the altar with [[Thick Skin]] on will restore 8 prayer points.

The order of the chairs, and the amount of prayer restored, hint towards the passcode for the chest in the western room: '''35158'''. Once the passcode is entered, you will receive the [[Jovkai key]].[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - trekking through Vampyrium.png|thumb|280x280px|The team treks through a Vampyrium forest.]]Make your way to the building with an anvil, enter through the Jovkai door from the south side, and take the [[old cog]]. Once you leave this house, [[Drakan]] will start pursuing the player at running speed, so wait until he is as far from you as possible before rushing back to Ivan and the group. Once you reach the group, you are safe from Drakan until proceeding. 

Before leaving, Ivan will reveal that he had acquired some supplies from the ruins. Alongside the aforementioned items found in the castle, he will also supply [[rancid slimy potion]]s and [[rank frothy potion]]s. These are the equivalent of [[Saradomin brew]]s and [[super combat potion]]s respectively, although the slimy potions drain combat stats by 1 rather than the larger amount brews penalise. Take as much as needed; then, speak to either Veliaf or Vanescula to initiate a cutscene where you all trek through the forests of Vampyrium.[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - avoiding spear lunges.mp4|thumb|400px|Drakan using his spear lunging attack. The marks of blood indicate where he'll strike, while the glimmering sparkle will indicate the safe tiles. Players must click on those tiles instantly to avoid the attack.]]

===First blood===
A cutscene will play, showing the group arriving at a [[Ruined Village]], where Drakan is waiting. Lowerniel will ask Vanescula if she remembered this place, and she tells them that it was where he killed their father, akin to putting down a beast, while Lowerniel felt as if it was him giving his father the honourable death he deserved. It's time for the first fight, during which you will be assisted by both Vanescula and Veliaf, but don't expect them to deal a lot of damage. Pray [[Protect from Melee]] and dodge the attack described below.

Drakan will immediately attack Vanescula. You will not be able to deal damage to him immediately; you must first dodge several of his lunging attacks. Once a few (3-5) spear strikes are dodged, you will become able to deal damage.

When Drakan focuses on you, he will use [[melee]] attacks and telegraphed spear attacks which will deal moderate damage if caught by one. During the spear attacks, he will draw a mark of blood into the left or right side of his body, indicating the tiles that he will strike. '''Opposite''' to the side the marks are absorbed, tiles will sparkle with a glimmer animation, these are the safe tiles. If you click on the safe tiles, at the right moment, you will dodge and roll out of the way. '''You will always need to step at least one tile back!'''

Once he is below 2,900 health, these sparkles no longer appear, and the player must rely on the mark of blood and their reaction time to avoid it.

The timing to dodge the spear attacks is extremely precise and requires input to be tick perfect. Drakan will glow red just before he lunges. This is the cue indicating when the player must move in order to avoid the attack. There is also a distinctive sound cue that indicates which tick to move. It is recommended for players to enable game sounds and gain familiarity with the sound cues in addition to the visual ones.

It is extremely helpful, in this fight as well as any subsequent fights to come, to keep the camera oriented from a high angle such that the player and Lowerniel are on the same vertical axis. This will give the best possible view of his signals prior to the dodge opportunity.

To the south, players can right click "quick escape" the encounter if they are to run low on supplies. If you escape the encounter, you will return to a forested area with a run-down tent, from which you can gather more supplies. 

Drakan starts with 3,000 health, but you only need to do 450 damage during this round. Upon hitting 85% of his health, a cutscene will ensue in which you all scatter into the forest and become separated from each other.
<!--Prey unlocks-->

===Over the river and through the woods===
Before leaving the area, resupply if needed, as you'll be fighting several monsters native to the forest. Upon leaving the safe area through the darkwood trees to the west, you will be attacked by two [[ancient feral vyre]]s. When fighting multiple of them at once, one will swap places with the other and begin healing, whilst forcing you to attack the vyre that took its place. Simply switch targets to resume attacking the initial vyre. Two more will spawn, who must also be slain before the encounter is complete.

The next section is an area with many choppable [[darkwood tree]]s that block the path. If you do not have an axe, take the [[bronze axe]] from the [[Stump (The Blood Moon Rises)|stump]] upon reaching this section. During this time, [[Tick (item)|ticks]] may crawl into your inventory and begin dealing 1 damage in fixed intervals; to remove them, simply find the tick in your inventory and click on it—alternatively, if you have a full inventory, then the ticks will not bite you. Odd trees with spikes around them will also deal damage if you stand next to them.

To fell a tree, it must be chopped from two different sides; you may need to jump over the tree stumps multiple times from different sides in order to reach another side of a tree. Chop your way until you reach the north-east corner of the area, from which you can enter the next part of the forest. Optionally, you may chop one of the darkwood trees at the southern end of the area to receive a [[rotten diary]].

The next section is an S- shaped pathway patrolled by [[maxilla beast]]s. They cannot be attacked, and will knock you and deal 30-50 damage if you are too close to them. Examining them will reveal that the beasts are blind; as such, their hearing is very strong, so players must also walk during this section or they will begin to run towards you. Follow the pathway until you reach the cave. As supplies are unlimited, players may wish to simply run through and eat along the way.
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - nylocas horde.png|thumb|280px|The player fights a horde of nylocas in their native environment.]]
The next section after you exit the cave is a face-off with a horde of [[nylocas]], who spawn from two corners. The [[Nylocas Ischyros|white ischyros]] must be attacked with [[melee]], while the [[Nylocas toxobolos|green toxobolos]] must be attacked with [[ranged]]. They behave the same way as their [[Theatre]] equivalents, becoming immune to attacks if attacked with the wrong style, and exploding if left alone long enough.

There are throwable [[Spine (The Blood Moon Rises)|spines]] on the ground which act as darts, so there is no need to re-gear for range. You can also harvest the [[dead venator]] for more spines if required. It is recommended to leave and return with fast hitting weapons, such as the [[toxic blowpipe]], if players are having trouble making it through this section.

The final section is a river crossing. Players must wrangle the three [[blood serpent]]s around the area; they can only be picked up whilst you are directly behind them; otherwise, they will deal 5 damage. Once you have picked up three (3) [[dead blood serpent]]s, use them on each other to create a [[serpent rope]]; then, use it on the [[Long branched tree (The Blood Moon Rises)|long branched tree]] to swing across the river.
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - meeting Efaritay.png|thumb|width=280x280|Efaritay comes to the rescue.]]

===Efaritay's aid===
[[File:Efaritay Hallow chathead.png|left|frameless]]
Upon entering the trees, a cutscene will play in which you emerge from the woods, with [[Drakan]] on coming out on the other side. He will argue that if he gets what he wants, then vampyres will no longer be present in [[Morytania]], freeing the humans from their rule. However, you will claim the cost to do so is too great, and that [[Vanescula]] already had plans in place before he shut it down. Drakan will refute this, claiming it was she who ceased operations. He will then draw his spear, but several [[aranei]] will appear and distract him, before a winged woman flies down and asks you to come with her.

Once you're safe, she will reveal herself as [[Efaritay Hallow]], Safalaan's mother and the former queen of [[Hallowvale]]. She will further tell you that she has rescued your companions, and that there is someone who wants to meet you. You both then enter a palace at the side of a mountain, where you find [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]] and [[Veliaf]]. You point out the resemblance of the mysterious strangers to the ones you've encountered during [[A Night at the Theatre]], and you will have an audience with a mysterious vampyre, claiming they're glad to finally speak with you in person.
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - Sugadinti Vitur.png|thumb|280px|The player meets the master of the mysterious stranger.]]
You will recognise them as the master of the mysterious strangers, and he'll formally introduce himself as [[Sugadinti Vitur]], the father of [[Verzik]]. He will tell you that he has remained in Vampyrium since before Drakan united the vampyre clans, and that despite his opposition, Verzik conspired with Drakan to kill Sugadinti in order to lead as head of House Vitur. He will then tell you that he has Vanescula imprisoned, as she smuggled [[daeyalt]] ore at some point during your escape from the castle, suggesting she may have other plans.

However, now that they've revealed themselves to Drakan, Sugadinti must now enact his plans to travel to Gielinor and trap Drakan in Vampyrium, a plan for which he'd been laying the groundwork for many years. You will be hesitant to trust another vampyre, but Efaritay will vouch for him, despite their differences.

==Hallowed Preparations==
You must now complete several short tasks to help prepare for Drakan's attack. Note that additional dialogue is available from many characters during this section.

{{Checklist|{{Checklist|title=Preparing the potion to cure Safalaan|
* First speak with Efaritay, who is preparing a potion to help Safalaan recover. She will ask that you make a stew mixed with amitire leaves from ingredients around the palace. 
* Exit the palace and pick the amitire plant to the east, then return inside
* A bowl can be found in the shelves next to the sink, with a potato and raw impaler meat being found in the cupboard by the western wall
* Use the bowl on the sink, then use the bowl of water on the potato
* Cook the meat at the range, then use it on the incomplete stew
* Cook the stew at the range, then finally add the leaves to create an amitire stew.
* Speak to Efaritay, then use the stew on Safalaan
}}}}

He will briefly become lucid, and [[Efaritay]] tells you that in time, he will return to normal. You will then ask for advice on [[Drakan]], to which she cannot offer much. However, she will make some recommendations on [[Hallowed flail|improving your blisterwood flail]], telling you that pure silvthrill, now only found in hallowed marks, is also effective. She will lastly recommend you shorten the flail's shaft and incorporate an enchanted diamond to further improve your flail, before giving you some hallowed marks for you to use.

=== Flailing around ===
{{Checklist|* Free up seven inventory spaces and then head to the east side of the palace. 
* Take all the tools from the workbench, then search the nearby crates for blisterwood logs and a blessed silver sickle. 
* Next, search both chests in the room for a diamond and an enchant diamond tablet
* Use the diamond and tablet on the sickle, in that order, to create an enchanted diamond sickle (b). 
* Use the logs on the sickle to create a blisterwood sickle (e)
* Lastly, upgrade the flail into a Hallowed flail by using the blisterwood sickle (e) on the anvil|title=Creating the Hallowed Flail}}After making the [[Hallowed flail|flail]], speak to [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]], who will introduce you to [[Sarei]], the stranger you assisted during [[A Night at the Theatre]]. They will explain why they could not take direct action or assist the Myreque, and follow up on your work in the Theatre. They will also advise you to craft some [[blisterwood stake]]s from the log stockpile; you must do this to progress; however, only one set of stakes (5) is required. Speak with Ivan afterwards to notify him you have done so. Lastly, head downstairs and speak to [[Veliaf]] and [[Vanescula]], who claims the daeyalt she smuggled was for insurance in case things went awry.

After finishing everything with your allies, speak to [[Sugadinti]], who will order the aranei to prepare for Drakan's arrival. You will offer your assistance in the defence, in spite of Sarei's objections, but he ultimately allows you to do so as long as you stick close to him.<!--The Bridge unlocks-->

==Drakan's Siege==
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - Drakan bridge fight.png|thumb|width=280x280|The aranei fearlessly attack Drakan.]]
Leave the palace to initiate a cutscene. You will offer your assistance in the defence, in spite of Sarei's objections, but they ultimately allow you to do so as long as you fall back when they order you to.

The bridge will be full of aranei, ready to defend the palace. [[Drakan]] will emerge from the forest and begin eliminating the aranei in front of him with frightening ease, before they manage to cast a barrier to stop him from going further. In response to the obstacle, Drakan simply raises his arm, conjuring numerous blood portals above that rain projectiles on the aranei. One of the aranei will try to shoot them down but will be quickly killed by the projectiles, leaving behind a [[silvthrill ballista]] and some [[silvthrill javelin]]s, which you notice and immediately pick up.
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - bridge defence.png|thumb|280px|The player assists the aranei in defending the bridge.]]
You will need to defend the aranei from the incoming portals with the ballista. The portals will always be one-shot, but they will eventually begin to spawn faster than you can shoot them down. You will still need to have some participation, or you will fail the defence; once actively participating up until the defender integrity reaches ~60%, you will be able to progress without any further actions. Once this occurs, the protective barrier dissipates and Sarei sends you back inside, fighting Drakan to the death.
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - palace defence.png|thumb|280px|The player assists Efaritay and the aranei in defending the palace entrance.]]
Afterward, [[Lowerniel]] will begin breaking through the palace doors. Some of the ceiling rubble will fall on one of the aranei holding [[Vanescula]], freeing her to kill the other. Upstairs, [[Efaritay]] will join the defence. Similarly to the bridge, you must have sufficient participation in this sequence, or you will fail and have to restart from the beginning. The events consist of rubble falling on aranei, stunning them, and cracks on the windows and front two pillars. Actively participating up until the hideout integrity reaches ~50% will be sufficient participation to progress.

=== Round two ===
[[Drakan]] will breach the palace, and you will have to once again fight him off. This time, the [[aranei]] and [[Efaritay]] will help you, but expect to pull your weight. Like the spear lunges from the first fight, he will begin incorporating targeted AoE attacks that the player will need quick reactions to. Efaritay will occasionally heal you and the aranei, and you can always grab more supplies from the supply table if you die or have to retreat. Drakan's attacks grow stronger the less HP he has left, his special attack ranging about 12-19 in the beginning, but rapidly increasing towards 40-50 by the end of the fight.

</gallery>

Drakan has 85% health (or 2550 HP) by the beginning of the fight, and the player will need reduce his health to 58% (or 1740 HP) so 810 HP in total in order to progress. A cutscene will ensue in which you and Efaritay retreat further into the hideout, but [[Lowerniel]] busts his way through while [[Vanescula]] attacks [[Safalaan]]. Surprised to see [[Sugadinti]], Lowerniel offers to let you go in return for either Efaritay or Safalaan. Efaritay refuses and tries to stop him, while Drakan casts a spell on the portal, expanding it and sending everyone to Gielinor.
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - The Blood Moon Rises.png|thumb|width=280x280|The blood moon rises.]]

== Another Night at the Theatre ==
You and [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]] will arrive at the [[Haunted Woods]], and see that the blood moon has risen on Gielinor as the vampyres begin bringing humans for the festival. You will reconvene with [[Veliaf]] and [[Sugadinti]] in [[Burgh de Rott]], where preparations will be made to bring the [[Nylocas Queen]] onboard as an ally, with Sugadinti ensuring she will comply. You and Sugadinti will head to the [[Theatre]], while Ivan and Veliaf will search for Vanescula's whereabouts.

[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - fighting Maiden.png|thumb|280px|The player battles the Maiden of Sugadinti once more.]]
Before you leave, you can ask Sugadinti various questions, such as whether you believe the Nylocas Queen will be of help or what he'll do if Drakan is deposed. Once you're ready, make your way to [[Ver Sinhaza]] and gear up for fight against several waves of enemies previously fought in the [[Theatre of Blood]]. They are significantly easier to fight than during [[A Night at the Theatre]], and should not prove an issue with sufficient supplies. '''{{Colour|red|Warning}}: Deaths during this section are treated like normal deaths'''; you will be sent to your [[respawn]] location and have to get back to your [[gravestone]] and pay any associated fees for reclaiming your items. As such, it is highly recommended that you bank your [[Drakan's medallion]] (or ensure that you have multiple) to make returning easier.

==Fighting Wyrds==
{{Map|x=3543|y=3258|mtype=square|caption=Location of the ruined building|align=right|r=3|height=200|width=280}}
Head to the ruined building north-east of [[Burgh de Rott]], then speak to [[Veliaf]] or [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]]. Upon entry, a cutscene will play in which you discover that the building is another vampyrification lab, and [[Vanescula]] has put [[Safalaan]] through the process; with his [[Icyene]] blood, the vampyrification process has transformed him into a monstrous [[wyrd]]. Too powerful for even Vanescula to handle, he knocks her and Veliaf back with ease.<!--I'm Sorry unlocks--> If you die while fighting Wyrd, you will be placed outside the laboratory with all your items intact. You can use the bank at Burgh de Rott as needed to resupply.

=== Fight mechanics ===
The wyrd has 1,100 health and will attack with [[melee]] that will push the player back one tile. [[Protect from Melee]] will significantly reduce the damage of his attacks, although if there is no tile behind the player to be pushed into, they will take light damage from the recoil. If using [[ranged]] to stay out of Wyrd's melee range, he is unable to perform any special attacks, but will instead use [[magic]] attacks the entire fight, which can hit up to 25 damage each and cannot be blocked by [[protection prayers]]. Players who can deal high damage per second may find this method superior to learning the melee mechanics. It is '''highly recommended''' to use quick-prayers for this fight, as this removes the need to switch tabs.

At the beginning of the fight, the wyrd attacks in a repeating cycle with two (2) melee attacks, a screech, another 2 melee attacks, another screech, then a double slam. This cycle repeats until around 60% health, where he will sometimes use a bloody screech in place of a regular screech.

==Night of the Blood Moon==
{{Needed|[[Combat equipment]], a [[prayer potion]], and a full inventory of [[food]].|recommended= [[Efaritay's aid]] to speed up kills.}}
Prepare for a third round against [[Drakan]]. Bring a full inventory of [[food]], as well as a [[prayer restore potion]]. [[Saradomin brew|Brews]] are not needed during this fight.

A cutscene will play in which Drakan will commence his speech, noting that the sacrifices his people have brought are not enough before noticing that [[Jovkai]] is nowhere to be seen after all he said previously. [[Lord Myrmel]] will claim that Jovkai had no interest in such a farce, and Drakan will commend his courage, believing that he would hide with him. Stating that he doesn't need his sister and is capable of adapting, he proceeds to immediately vaporise Myrmel into a bloody pulp, using his blood along with Efaritay's to power a portal back to Vampyrium. As this happens, you, [[Sugadinti]] and [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]] will arrive and confront him. Drakan states that he has the ability to rectify all his failings right now, and Sugadinti tells him that his daughter isn't here to stop him this time. Taking it as a hollow threat, Drakan claims that he doesn't need her, and Sugadinti clarifies that he isn't fighting him alone as the [[Nylocas Queen]] enters the courtyard. Intrigued, Drakan will assume a combat stance, releasing Efaritay from his hold.

=== Round three ===
This fight is arguably easier than the previous, as [[Efaritay]], [[Ivan Strom|Ivan]], [[Sugadinti]], the [[Nylocas Queen]], and her [[nylocas]] will all assist in damaging [[Drakan]]. You will still need to pull your weight, but you will receive substantially more help, and Efaritay and Ivan will both heal you periodically. The mechanics for this fight are the same as before; however, the blood swipes will now take place three (3) times, and Drakan will begin firing an additional orb after every special attack.

The small stage for this fight means that it's easy to take damage when backed into a wall. Try to remain in an area where you can move at least three (3) tiles back, and run to the other side of Drakan if needed. If you need to escape, the castle doors to the east can be used; if you die during this fight, you will respawn by [[Veliaf]]. Players who die or teleport out can return to the fight by talking to him. Once Drakan reaches ~30% of his health (900 hitpoints), a cutscene will trigger in which [[Safalaan]], having progressed further into his [[wyrd]] form, attacks Drakan and rips one of his wings off, then tackles him into the portal. Sugadinti will then quickly close the portal, believing that Drakan is permanently trapped as he cannot use Safalaan's now-tainted blood to return. Efaritay, however, refuses to believe this and leaves.

Sugadinti will ask that you wait for him inside the castle whilst he addresses the vampyres. They will accept him as their ruler, and will ask Ivan and Veliaf to travel to Misthalin to reassure the kingdom that war will not be on the table. Meanwhile, you will be tasked with finding Efaritay, with Sugadinti saying that saving Safalaan's life cannot be done at the risk of Drakan's return.

Efaritay can be found in the [[Icyene Graveyard]], where the player will tell her that they are going to [[Vampyrium]] with her, at which point she will create a portal.

The player should come through the portal with their best [[melee setup]] including the '''mandatory''' [[hallowed flail]]. Drakan has significantly higher ranged defence, and there is no Vampyrium equivalent to [[ranging potions]], so using [[blisterwood stake]]s is not recommended. As before, the player's damage is capped between 26-28 damage per hit.

=== Preparing for the final battle ===
After stepping through the portal, [[Safalaan]] will be found in the {{FloorNumber|uk=2}} of the castle, with his [[wyrd]] transformation progressing. The player tells [[Efaritay]] to get Safalaan to [[Morytania]] and promises her to deal with [[Drakan]]. After the cutscene, Drakan awaits on the top of the castle, accessible via the northern door. As with two of the previous fights with Drakan, Vampyrium supplies are provided in the [[Chest (The Blood Moon Rises)|chest]] just outside the door which leads to the fight:

The jar of congealed blood should '''always''' be taken for emergency healing, often needed in Phase 3 when Drakan's combos reach their highest tempo and the environment can disable [[Protect from Melee]]. '''Two''' rank frothy potions ('''green''') should be taken to keep combat boosts high. '''Three to four''' foul chunky potions ('''pink''') should be taken to restore prayer. The '''remaining slots''' should be rancid slimy potions ('''yellow''') for healing. The final fight is fairly long and therefore the [[rancid slimy potion]] is preferred over the jerky and kebab as it allows for vastly more hitpoints restored per inventory space. The potion also has a shorter attack delay than the jerky. 

Players can prepot the fight by dropping a full yellow, pink, and green potion on the ground. They should then sip potions in their inventory in that order, yellow, pink, and green, drop those partially full remainders, and pick up the full ones left on the ground at the beginning. This will allow the player to start the fight overhealed with the maximum possible combat stat bonuses. 

The player must remain mindful that with each heal from the yellow potion, their Attack and Strength will drop by one. Continue to use pink and green potions to keep those stats boosted. Keeping these stats higher for as long as possible is more important in the first two phases than keeping the player's health above 60.

An [[Efaritay's aid]] will raise the player's DPS against Drakan. A fresh ring should last nearly the entire length of the fight. However, as the player can only use the supply chest to deposit to their bank and not withdraw, the player must either sacrifice inventory slots for spare rings or teleport out and return for each attempt. It is recommended to use a non-degradable ring at least until the player can consistently reach Phase 3. That said, Efaritay's aid is not essential for success for most setups. Note that a [[Black mask]]/[[Slayer helmet]] with a vampyre task does '''NOT''' increase damage or accuracy.

Drakan is immune to [[Life leech|life-leech]], recoil, venom and poison damage. [[Thralls]] cannot be summoned during the fight.

If you die while fighting Drakan, you will be placed with full health and prayer by the door leading to the fight with any remaining supplies you had. There are no death fees and more supplies may be taken from the chest. However, you must start over from the beginning of the fight. If you teleport away from the fight or supply room, you will need to return to the Icyene Graveyard by boat and re-enter the portal. 	
[[File:Blood Moon Rises - Drakans last dance.gif|thumb|width=289x289|Drakan regenerates his wing with haemalchemy as he readies to perform his last hunt.]]
Much of the fight will be spent executing dodges. Drakan's signals prior to each attack will increase in tempo with each phase. The player will also be required to execute precise running movement, switch [[protection prayers]], and both avoid environmental hazards and learn to dodge another special attack later in the fight. Similar to prioritising switching protection prayers when fighting [[TzTok-Jad]] in the [[TzHaar Fight Cave]], the player must prioritise seeing the dodge patterns in order to survive. Healing or using another potion only '''once''' per attack is recommended. That said, perfect play is not required: there are only a few consistent points in the fight in which mistakes are harshly punished. Beyond the dodge mechanics practised in the previous encounters, the fight is relatively straightforward. However the length of the fight and the sustained concentration required will challenge many players.
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - the final confrontation.png|thumb|291x291px|The final confrontation with Drakan.]]
Players should activate [[Protect from Melee]] and [[Piety]] immediately on beginning the fight. During the prolonged special attacks sections which begin phases two and three, neither one is essential to keep on, and the player will need to activate [[Protect from Magic]] once those sections end. 

Once again, players struggling to see which direction to dodge in should keep the camera oriented from a high angle such that the player and Drakan are on the same vertical axis. This will give the best possible view of his signals priors to the dodge opportunity. Using true tile for both the player and the boss can also be very helpful.

===Phase 1===
Drakan's health is restored to 3,000. He has three distinct phases. Each phase has roughly 1,000 hitpoints, with his attacks speeding up with each phase. He will use his spear combos and his two area of effect attacks (front/back and semicircle) from the previous three fights. Once at around 2,700 health, he will begin to use four attacks in his combos which also incorporate the slam attack. He will also intermittently attack the player with normal melee, dealing unavoidable chip damage even with prayer. Drakan's successful hits, including the chip damage, will slightly heal him throughout the fight. If you find that you're having trouble timing Drakan's spear attacks, focus on the red visual highlight before his combo attack starts, since clicking to dodge before that will lead to you taking hits. Because of the precise timing required, it can be worth it to quick escape through the stairs and do this first section over several times until you feel comfortable with your ability to reliably dodge the combo attack, as it will return slightly faster in later phases. You don't need to be perfect, but you do need to dodge the majority of damage to still have brews at the end. A good first phase should use between 2-4 brews.

The area of effect attacks tend be used in clusters. There is a subtle visual and audio cue between the front/back attack and the semicircle, and the semicircle has a significantly longer charging period. When charging for the semicircle, Drakan will hold his spear in front of his chest. When charging for the front/back attack, the spear will be held at his side. If the attack is the semicircle, click well beyond Drakan's character model to avoid clicking the elongated hitbox of his charge.

It is important to stay mindful of the space behind the player after each attack. Dodges that have been clicked correctly will fail if the player cannot move backwards. If there are fewer than three or four tiles of space behind the player after a dodge sequence, immediately move 90 degrees to an adjacent side of Drakan before his next combo begins. You can also move to his far side by passing through him, but this is riskier because he might start his attack wind up while you're running so stepping around one of his corners to change sides is preferred. If passing through him, you should click two spaces past Drakan because he will try to follow you and can intercept you so that you wind up on an adjacent side instead. Remember to always reposition the camera while moving to see the next combo pattern.

To simplify things, remember that after Drakan performs an explosion/ground slam attack, further attacks will always be in an alternating pattern. For example: left, slam, right, left.<gallery mode="packed" heights="400" style="text-align:centre">
The Blood Moon Rises - Drakan 4 way combo.mp4|Once Drakan is below 2,700 health, he may begin using the spear lunge attack four times.
The Blood Moon Rises - Drakan final spear specials.mp4|Drakan using two different type of spear cleaves. The player dodges them perfectly, alongside the spear lunges that come after.
</gallery>

===Phase 2===
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - Drakan blood wave dodging.mp4|thumb|400px|The player dodges the blood waves during the second phase of the fight.]]
Once Drakan drops below 2100 hitpoints, he will vanish from the arena and flood the eastern side of the roof with blood pools. Twelve portals will spawn outside the arena, four each to the north, east and south which will discharge solid walls of blood waves in a set pattern. These waves deal moderate damage and disable overhead prayers.

Damage from the wave can be evaded by running straight toward them. True tile is very helpful to understand the player's true position relative to the waves. Ideally, the player should be moving past the wave by four tiles. The player must try to run as straight as possible. Avoid spam clicking, and ensure you are confident with your clicks to avoid unnecessary diagonal or extra pathing. Moving diagonally will cause the player not to dodge the wave and take damage, as will running away from the wave or being caught standing still. There is a brief cooldown period after being hit by a wave where other waves won't deal damage. At the beginning of the phase, it is recommended to turn the camera to face east, or directly over head, and zoom out a considerable amount so that they can see all the waves on screen at once. With the camera east, the blood pools will be at the top of the screen. From this angle, the waves will come from the left, right, and top of the screen in the following set pattern: left, right, top, left, right, left, top, pincer (left and right simultaneously), then the preceding sequence again before finishing with left, top, and right. At the beginning of the sequence, it's recommended to run as far west (i.e., toward the camera) as possible to have enough time to avoid the downward waves.

As soon as the last blood wave is crossed, Drakan will reappear and sacrifice between 80 and 110 of his own hitpoints to launch four blood strikes at the player. These appear as red projectiles that will strike the player all at once. These will deal 80+ damage which will likely be '''fatal''' if not blocked with [[Protect from Magic]]. The player must have the prayer active before the projectiles reach them. If you find it difficult to notice Drakan when he appears, consider highlighting him as an NPC so he has a stronger outline to announce his arrival.

The player should then immediately switch back to [[Protect from Melee]] as Drakan will approach and issue a combo attack which, if dodged perfectly, will guarantee that the player deals 155 damage on their next hit. If the player succeeds at this, the blood wave sequences will end and normal combat will resume. If the player is not successful, the blood waves, red projectiles, and combo attack sequence will play out up to two more times, or three times total.

After the blood waves finish or are skipped, Drakan will return for combat until the next phase begins. For the first few minutes, Drakan will weave in magic attacks consisting of a single red projectile. The player must switch to Protect from Magic again to avoid taking up to 20 damage. Once the zero hitsplat appears, return to Protect from Melee. Around 1500 hitpoints, Drakan will stop using his blood magic attack and focus on using his full combo attack again. You will know you're still in the blood magic phase if Drakan is using simple two or three hit combo attacks without the slam attack. Once the blood magic phase ends, Drakan will start using four hit combo attacks with slams. As soon as this happens, make sure you're in Protect from Melee and then switch back to your inventory tab to brew through any damage taken. Now is also a good time to reup your free super combat boost because this phase of the fight will last for 500 more hitpoints. The combo attack telegraph animation will run a little faster here so it's important not to complacently use the same timing you did for the attacks in phase one off muscle memory. Pay visual attention to Drakan and move when his red outline appears. Around 1250(?) hitpoints, Drakan will add his wind up spear cleave attack from before to the rotation, but now the single red orb lunge he does after the AoE is two red orbs on the same side. Click a tile back twice on the opposite side to dodge them. In terms of meta-strategy, it's important to make sure you can dodge a good portion of the attacks in this phase, ideally at least half, so that you go into phase three with a good number of brews and the blood pot remaining.

===Phase 3===
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - Drakan dash.mp4|thumb|400px|The player dodges Drakan's spear dash during the third phase of the fight.]]
After dropping below 900 hitpoints, Drakan will vanish from the arena once more. Blood pools will spawn around the arena and lightning will also randomly strike, preceded by a circular, dark grey shadow. If you step onto a blood pool, you will take heavy damage and your overhead protection prayer will be disabled. Lightning will also disable overhead prayers. Initially, during this phase, Drakan cannot be targeted, and will appear at inconsistent intervals to deliver a 3x5 AoE spear lunge attack. These attacks will be preceded by him appearing briefly three times facing the player around a 90-degree rotation, with the final direction marking the direction of his attack. For example, he might briefly appear in the east and then swing around 90 degrees to attack you from the north. This attack will deal 20-30 damage, but is avoidable by moving 2-5 tiles perpendicular to his attack direction, for example by moving east or west if the attack is coming from the north. To consistently hit this dodge, stand mostly still while minding the lightning bolts, and immediately click in the direction where Drakan ''first'' appears. If you have trouble processing Drakan's initial spawn location, it's okay; there's a slight delay before the attack and you can still dodge by clicking a few tiles away in a direction that will move you out of Drakan's line of sight. Your character will perform a roll that dodges the attack. This seems to not work if you click too far away from your current position, so be mindful to click 2-5 tiles away from where you're currently standing. If you fail the dodge, eat before he appears again. Keep in mind that if Drakan appears while you're moving, it will be almost impossible to dodge his attack, so you want to move the minimal amount necessary to dodge the lightning and blood pools. Unlike the blood waves, some diagonal movement is tolerated for a successful dodge. Normal pathing mechanics do not apply when dodging the attacks, as the player can move more than two (2) tiles at once. So, if there is a blood pool two tiles away from the player in the direction they must dodge, they can click beyond the blood pool and still be safe.

Similarly to the end of each blood wave sequence, following the four lunges, Drakan will reappear and sacrifice some of his health to again launch four enhanced blood strikes, which must be blocked with Protect from Magic. Just as before, Drakan will use a combo attack to follow up. If dodged perfectly, the player will deal a guaranteed 80 damage on the next hit. Unlike the blood wave phase, successful dodges and punish hits after the blood strikes will not skip the remaining lunges. In total, Drakan will perform the lunge sequence followed by the blood strikes three (3) times.

When all three of his lunge attack sequences are finished, Drakan will resume normal combat at a slightly faster tempo. Unlike the beginning of Phase 2, he will not issue any single blood strikes, which require flicking to Protect from Magic, but the blood pools and random lightning strikes will persist and continue to deal damage and disable overhead prayer, so the player must be mindful of them as they dodge. Always ensure Protect from Melee is enabled before Drakan attacks again. Because of the high damage that may be incurred from dropping prayer, it is recommended to save the jar of congealed blood for this phase to heal back to full health in an emergency. If you're on track to win, you should still have several brews remaining by this stage. If you and Lowerniel each hit 0 hitpoints at the same time, it will count as your victory. You will reappear in the castle - simply walk through the northern door to activate the cutscene. 

===The sun rises===
Once Lowerniel hits 0 hitpoints, a cutscene will trigger in which he stumbles away from you in pain, looking and reaching out to the blood moon before collapsing and dying from his injuries. You will take the [[Sunspear]] from his corpse and return to Gielinor, where Safalaan's wyrd transformation has fully completed. Safalaan will beg you and Efaritay to kill him, but both of you refuse, and Safalaan will relent, thanking both of you for not abandoning and giving up on him. You will offer the Sunspear back to Efaritay, who refuses and allows you to keep it, as she is tired of fighting, while she herself decides to oversee her son's affliction with potions and rituals. As the two leave, you will stare out into the ocean as a new sun rises in the horizon, an indicator that all of your efforts in saving Morytania have not gone to waste.

==Historical==
In ''RuneScape 3'', the Myreque questline concludes with two quests: {{RSL|The Lord of Vampyrium}}, which bears many similarities to The Blood Moon Rises, and {{RSL|River of Blood}}, about [[Vanescula Drakan]] becoming leader of the vampyres. Some notable differences between the two questlines include:
* Lowerniel only loses one wing in ''Old School'', being torn off by Safalaan before his final fight. In ''RuneScape 3'', both of his wings are ripped off by Vanescula before the final phase of the fight.
* In both games, [[Safalaan Hallow|Safalaan]] is turned into a [[wyrd]]. However, in ''RuneScape 3'', he willingly chose to do so, and his hunger and inability to shapeshift back into human form is cured with the player's assistance through an {{RSL|Extreme Guthix balance}}. In ''Old School'', his transformation into a wyrd is done against his will, he cannot currently shapeshift, and his hunger is not fully cured, with [[Efaritay]] beginning to research rituals and potions to help him.
* In ''Old School'', a large portion of Vampyrium is explored during and after the quest, while in ''RuneScape 3'', only Castle Drakan is visited. In ''RuneScape 3'', it is planned for Vampyrium to be accessible during the {{RSL|Sanguine quest series}}.
** [[Venator]]s are encountered in both games, but other creatures of Vampyrium only appear in ''Old School''. While they are considered to be the devolved form of vampyres due to exposure from the Sanguine in ''RuneScape 3'', in ''Old School'', the remaining vyres on the planet devolved into an [[Ancient feral vyre|feral state]], while venators themselves had been bred for sport and hunting.
* Efaritay spends time as a prisoner of Lord Drakan in both questlines, but in ''RuneScape 3'' she is freed after sensing Drakan's death by the player, while in ''Old School'', she was freed with the help of [[Sugadinti]] and joins his cause.
* Sugadinti and his disciples do not appear in ''RuneScape 3'', nor does the player fight Drakan solo. Instead, Drakan is defeated with the assistance of Vanescula and the Myreque, the majority of the latter perishing in the attempt. In ''Old School'', the deaths of the Myreque is instead adapted as part of the [[Sins of the Father]].
** In ''RuneScape 3'', the player finishes off Drakan directly. In ''Old School'', the player allows him to walk off before he succumbs to his injuries.
* Drezel remains alive in ''Old School'', while in ''RuneScape 3'' he is fatally injured by Safalaan in his Wyrd form.
* In ''RuneScape 3'', Vanescula becomes the leader of the vampyres after Lowerniel's death, and then attempts to invade [[Misthalin]]. After this fails, she forms a treaty with Misthalin, and rules Morytania alongside Efaritay and Safalaan, with Veliaf and Aeonisig Raispher as advisors. 
** In ''Old School'', Veliaf decides to settle down in Burgh de Rott, reopening the local bar while wanting to have nothing more to do with the vyres. In ''RuneScape 3'', he chose to stay to guide Safalaan and preventing Vanescula from causing mischief.
** Vanescula is harmed by Lowerniel in ''RuneScape 3'', being impaled in the wing by the Sunspear and knocked unconscious, though her injury was minor. When Safalaan appears, she orders him to back off but he refuses. In ''Old School'', Vanescula is instead swatted away by a newly-transformed Safalaan which severely injures her.
** In ''Old School'', Vanescula's plans after defeating Lowerniel are not revealed. In ''RuneScape 3'', it is revealed that she planned to end the shortage of blood by using Safalaan's icyene blood to cross the River Salve and invade Misthalin, with the larger population of humans meaning blood tithes would be lighter and less frequent, like in the days of the [[Zarosian Empire]].
** In ''RuneScape 3'', the blood shortage is resolved in the short term by Vanescula moving blood stores from Vampyrium and the creation of a cure for Vampyrism for human-born vyres, with longer-term plans to conduct voluntary tithing. In ''Old School'', Sugadinti's aranei followers donate blood in the short term while they work on creating artificial blood via haemalchemy as a long term solution.
** In ''RuneScape 3'', the werewolves openly rebel against Vanescula's rule, while in ''Old School'', their status is left more ambiguous.
** Vyres still remain aggressive to the player in ''RuneScape 3'' if they aren't wearing a full set or mix of Darkmeyer or House Drakan robes, whereas vyres in ''Old School'' become tolerant of the player after the third fight against Lowerniel, with adjusted dialogue. 
** When Sugadinti sends Ivan and Veliaf to inform King Roald of the truce, the player may speak to him after the quest, during which Roald mistakenly believes that they were just fearmongering him. In ''RuneScape 3'', he personally saw the incident at the river and agreed to a truce, while secretly stockpiling large amounts of blisterwood in the event that the alliance collapsed. He consequently sends Aeonisig to Morytania as his representative due to his constant complaining.
* In ''RuneScape 3'', [[Ivandis Seergaze]] does not face Lowerniel Drakan after learning he is transforming into a vampyre, but rather seals himself in the [[Coffin (Priest in Peril)|coffin]] on the top floor of [[Paterdomus Temple]] to prevent himself from harming anyone, perishing when the [[River Salve]] is enchanted in {{RSL|River of Blood}}. In ''Old School'', his fate after learning of his vampyrification is left unknown.
* After the quest, Ivan speaks of searching for a columbarium (a structure holding cremated remains) under Paterdomus Temple. In ''RuneScape 3'', this columbarium is unlocked during the events of {{RSL|Legacy of Seergaze}}.
* In ''RuneScape 3'', the monks of Zamorak in the Paterdomus Temple were part of a joint Saradominist-Zamorakian {{RSL|Morytanian splinter group}} to remove the Edicts of Guthix. This splinter group is not present in ''Old School''.

==Trivia==
* The Blood Moon Rises is the second quest released in ''Old School'' to complete a quest line from the original game, after ''[[Song of the Elves]]'' in 2019. The quest effectively mirrors the ''[[rsw:RuneScape|RuneScape]]'' quest ''{{RSL|The Lord of Vampyrium}}'' as well as certain aspects of ''{{RSL|River of Blood}}''. Additionally, the mansion segment of the quest seems to take inspiration from the ''RuneScape'' quest ''{{RSL|Broken Home}}'', which is in turn heavily inspired by the mansion from the game ''{{wp|Resident Evil (1996 video game)|Resident Evil}}''.
* The Blood Moon Rises was originally announced at [[Summit#RuneFest_Summit_2025|RuneFest 2025]] and passed a poll in [[Poll:RuneFest 2025 Summit|March 2025]], with the rewards being polled separately following the [[Summit#Winter_Summit_2026|Winter Summit]] in [[Poll:The Winter Summit Poll|January 2026]].
* The release of Blood Moon Rises was scheduled for 11am UTC, however the game worlds were taken offline at 10:45am UTC to investigate an accuracy-related bug, delaying the release of the quest until 12:15pm UTC.
* A pop-up is given upon attempting to start the quest which outlines a number of suggested game settings for an optimal gameplay experience, and allows the user to automatically switch to those settings. These are:
** Master Volume - 100%
** Music Volume - 20% or greater
** Sound Effects Volume - 45% or greater
** Area Sounds Volume - 25% or greater
** Music Mode - Area
** View Distance - 50 or greater
* Upon release, the quest set the new record for highest skill requirements in [[Cooking]], [[Fletching]], [[Slayer]], [[Smithing]], and [[Woodcutting]] to obtain a [[Quest point cape]].
* During the quest, Lowerniel Drakan says, "The weak must die so that the strong may survive.  It is how every race operates, even yours.  There is no alternative."  This mirrors the Last Rites from the [[Zamorakian]] [[Unholy Book]], "The weak deserve to die, so the strong may flourish. This is the creed of Zamorak."
*The section where the player flees through the [[Sotfa Forest]] is at least partially inspired by the [[Temple Trekking]] minigame unlocked earlier in the Myreque series.
